:::{#def-strict-superset}
#### Strict superset

A set $B$ is a **strict superset** of a set $A$,
written $B \supsetneq A$,
if $B$ is a [superset](#def-superset) of $A$
and $B \neq A$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-strict-superset-subset}
#### Strict superset and strict subset

$B \supsetneq A$ means the same thing as $A \subsetneq B$
([strict subset](#def-strict-subset)).
For example, $\set{1, 2, 3} \supsetneq \set{1, 3}$,
because $\set{1, 2, 3}$ contains $2$ and $\set{1, 3}$ does not.

:::
